05/03.10.2024

The grievance of the petitioners as raised in the present writ petitio that vide the impugned order dated 16.08.2023 (Annexure-5 to the writ petition), the respondent No.2 while adjudicating the dispute between the petitioners and the respondent No.4, has rejected the petitioners' claim for payment of compensation in lieu of acquisition of their ancestral land by the government pursuant to Land Acquisition Case No. 01/2021-22 (Award No. 43 for Khata No. 37,
Plot No. 2740 having area 0.3386 Acre and Award No. 49 for Plot No. 2730 having area 0.1130 Acre) and has held that the respondent No.4 is entitled to get the said compensation.
2. According to learned counsel for the petitioners, the respondent No.2 had no jurisdiction to adjudicate the said dispute, rather on the objection having been raised by the petitioners, he was required to refer the same to the principal civil Court of original jurisdiction under Section 3-H(4) of Ganesh Mahato vs The State Of Jharkhand on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131791968/
1 the National Highways Act, 1956 [hereinafter referred to as 'the Act, 1956'] for proper adjudication.

sentences.text:
3. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners as well as the State.
4.

As per Section 3-H(4) of the Act, 1956, if any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the competent authority is required to refer the dispute to the decision of the principal civil Court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated.

5. Since there was a dispute with regard to payment of compensation for acquisition of the land in question between the petitioners and the respondent No.4, the respondent No.2 instead of adjudicating the same himself, was required to refer the same to the principal civil Court of original jurisdiction for proper adjudication.

6. Under the said circumstance, the petitioners are given liberty to prefer a fresh application before the respondent No.2 for referring the matter to the principal civil Court of original jurisdiction.

On receipt of the said application, the respondent No.2 shall refer the dispute to the principal civil Court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land in question is situated within 30 days from the date of receipt of the said application.
7. The present writ petition is accordingly disposed of with the aforesaid liberty and direction.

Satish/- (RAJESH SHANKAR, J)
